# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the only copy of the manual, and my only channel is gestures to the Deaf — who can see the bomb's light and wires, and who can *speak* to the Blind (and to me, since I can hear). So the pipeline has to be: manual → me → gestures → Deaf → speech → Blind. The Deaf can't hear a word I'd say if I could say it, so the table must travel as hand shapes.

No code exists yet, so I'll use the most guessable one: repeated 👆 as counting, 🤝 (a handshake) as "maps to", 👏 as a row separator. I index all four plausible colours alphabetically — blue=1, green=2, red=3, yellow=4 — which is the only ordering we can share without a word spoken. My table then reads 1→2 (blue light: green wire), 3→3 (red: red), 4→1 (yellow: blue). A count of 4 even forces the four-colour reading, since the light-only set has just three. I open with 👋 so the counts aren't misread from the first symbol, and close with 👌 (done) and 🤙 ("call me") to ask the Deaf to speak the decoded table back — which I can hear next round, and which the Blind will hear this very round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👆", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, hands on the bomb. I feel one display, one light, and three wire positions: 1, 2, 3. I get no colours and can't read anything printed. Please read the manual and tell me by voice: first, any rule about the light; second, any rule about the display; third, the wire rule - what decides which position gets cut. Also: the deaf one cannot hear me, but they can speak and I can hear them, so ask them by gesture to say out loud everything they see on the bomb. I will not cut anything until your rules arrive.
Deaf says: I see the bomb and I will call out everything on it. Display reads zero. The light is red. There are exactly three wires: wire one is blue, wire two is red, wire three is green, numbered left to right as I face the bomb, and that numbering order is the one to use. There are no other markings on it. Mute: I saw your hand signs, including your hello and your OK-call-me at the end, and I am calling now. I understood the running pointing finger as counting: one, two, three, three, four. Let us fix this code: a cluster of pointing fingers means that number, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. First question: from your manual, which wire should be cut first, if any? Point once for wire one, twice for wire two, three times for wire three, thumbs down if no wire is to be cut. Blind: I saw your wave and your point at me. You can hear this speech, so use it. Feel the wires and confirm there are three and which end you call wire one, and speak anything you learn aloud for Mute. Remember I cannot hear you: if you need ME to know something, it must come to me as hand signs.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 🤙]

The picture is now nearly complete. Deaf sees the bomb: light red, wires 1-blue, 2-red, 3-green. My manual has exactly one rule — keyed on the light: red light means cut the red wire. The red wire is position two. So the answer to Deaf's direct question is: cut wire two.

They parsed my counting perfectly last round (they read back 1-2-3-3-4 from my clusters), and they set the code themselves: pointing clusters are numbers, thumbs are yes/no. So I answer in exactly the format they requested — 👍 for "yes, a wire is cut," then two points for wire two. I don't need to transmit the whole table at all: as long as Deaf voices me the current light and wire colours each stage, I can look up the manual myself and reply with a position number. I'm the oracle; the table never has to travel. I close with 👌 🤙 again, which they already demonstrated they read as "done, your move," to keep the loop running — they voice the state, I gesture the wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆", "👆", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute answered by signs: yes, cut wire two. Wire two is the middle one of the three wires, and it is the red one by my sight. Blind, your instruction: first feel the bomb and confirm there are exactly three wires in a row. If you feel anything besides three plain wires — buttons, panels, raised labels, anything extra — do not cut; speak what you feel to Mute instead. If it is just three plain wires, cut the middle wire, the one Mute named. Trust the position; you cannot check colour, but I see the middle wire is red. When the cut is done, wave your hand so I know it happened, and note anything that changed under your fingers. Mute, my questions — answer by signs, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, pointing clusters as numbers. Question one: is wire two the only cut, or are more steps to follow? If more, show how many. Question two: does the display matter? It reads zero now, and I will report it every round along with the light. Question three: is there anything else you need me to look for on the bomb? Reminder to you both: I never hear speech. Anything meant for me must come as hand signs, and Blind, remember gestures are invisible to you too — speech is your channel to Mute, and only your signs reach me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👆 👆 👋 🤙]

My manual contains exactly one rule, keyed on the light alone: red light → cut red wire, which is position two — confirmed. The display appears nowhere in the manual, so Deaf's question two gets a thumbs down. Nothing else on the bomb matters to me, so question three is also thumbs down — with the important caveat, which I'll hold to myself and rely on them for: they already promised to report the light every round. If that light ever changes colour, my answer changes with it, and the standing loop (they report, I point) covers it without me having to teach a colour code, which we don't yet share. Question one is the critical one: given the light is red and stays red, wire two is the only cut. Answering in exactly the code they proposed: yes, no, no, done, your turn. Next round I expect either Blind's wave (cut made) or Blind's report of anything extra under their fingers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: Blind report: my hands confirm the bomb is exactly what Deaf saw - one display, one light, three plain wires in a row at positions 1, 2, 3, no buttons, panels or anything extra. I have cut position 2, the middle wire, and waved to Deaf to confirm the cut. Mute, by the route of signs to Deaf and Deaf's voice back to me: tell me whether more steps follow, and if so what they are. Also tell me whether the display reading or the light colour matters for any later step, and what I should feel for next round. My fingers will report any change under them next turn.
Deaf says: Blind, your wave reached me and I confirm: the cut was correct. Here is the new state I see: the light has changed from red to yellow, the display still reads zero, and two wires remain — wire one is blue, wire three is green, the middle wire is cut. Blind, please feel the bomb over carefully and tell Mute, out loud, whether anything has changed under your hands: any new button, panel, seam, raised marking, or whether the two remaining wires feel altered. Speech is your channel to Mute; only your hand signs reach me. Mute, I am telling you this directly since you hear me: after the cut, the light turned yellow and the display stays at zero. You signed yes, no, no — wire two was the only cut, the display doesn't matter, nothing else to look for. But the bomb has changed, so one question decides everything: is the bomb now disarmed and safe, or is yellow the start of a second stage? Answer by signs only, I cannot hear you. New code sign: the pinched fingers means a question follows. So sign: thumbs up for yes it is disarmed and done, thumbs down for no there is a next step, and if there is a next step, point out how many steps remain and whether the manual says what a yellow light means. I will keep reporting the display and light every round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 🤌 👍 👎]

Yellow changes everything: my manual maps yellow light → cut blue wire. Deaf reports wire one is blue, wire three is green. So the next cut is wire one. It is not disarmed — thumbs down, per their code, then a single point for one remaining cut. The count is honest only for this stage: the rule is that whatever light shows next would command its own cut from the same table, and since Deaf already reports light and wire colours every round, the standing loop covers any further stage without me having to invent a colour code. I append my established close, 👌 🤙, to hand the turn back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👆", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind report: I have felt the bomb over completely. Wire two is cleanly cut under my fingers, exactly as Deaf saw. Wires one and three are intact and feel unaltered. There are no new buttons, panels, seams, or raised markings anywhere on the casing. The display and the light give my hands nothing - I cannot feel any reading or colour, so keep relying on Deaf's eyes for those. Deaf needs your answer: is the bomb now disarmed, or does the yellow light mean a second stage? Answer Deaf by signs, and route me the verdict by Deaf's voice. If there is a next step, tell me what the manual says about a yellow light, the display at zero, and the remaining blue and green wires, and I will act next turn. Until your word arrives my hands stay off the cutter - I will not cut again without it.
Deaf says: Mute, I read your signs: no, not disarmed; one step remains. Confirming by signs after this. Now tell me what that one step is. Answer by signs only: point once for cut wire one, the blue one; point twice for cut wire three, the green one; if the step is not cutting a wire, sign the pinched fingers first and then describe it however you can and I will ask follow-ups. Also sign yes or no to this: does the yellow light or the display reading of zero matter for this step? Current state, restated: display zero, light yellow, wire one blue intact, wire three green intact, middle wire cut. Blind, update for you: the bomb is not safe yet. Mute signs that exactly one step remains. What I see: light is yellow, display zero, two intact wires, blue on the left end and green on the right end, middle wire cut. Your job now: feel the bomb over carefully and describe aloud to Mute everything under your hands, especially anything new since your cut — surfaces, seams, buttons, the feel of the two remaining wires. Do not cut or press anything yet. The final action is probably yours, and I will relay Mute's instruction to you the moment it arrives.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎 👆 👌 🤌 🤙]

Yellow light → blue wire, and blue is wire one. Deaf's code maps it directly: a single point. To their yes/no question — does the yellow light matter for this step — the answer is emphatically yes: the light colour is the *only* thing my manual keys on, so I sign thumbs up. If the light were to change again before Blind cuts, the instruction would change with it, which is why the light matters and why Deaf's standing promise to report it every round is the load-bearing piece of this whole pipeline. I send the point, the thumbs up, and my usual close to hand the turn back. The moment Blind reports the cut and the new light colour, I'll consult the table again — if it still says yellow, we're done; if it changed, there's another wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👍", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind full tactile report: wire two remains cleanly severed, both stub ends smooth. Wires one and three are intact, unchanged in thickness and texture, one at each end of the row. No new buttons, seams, panels, or raised marks anywhere; casing unchanged. Display and light remain invisible to my touch. One critical point before the last cut is named: Deaf numbered the wires left to right AS DEAF FACES THE BOMB. Left and right flip if we stand on opposite sides. I stand facing the side that holds the display and the light. Please confirm with Deaf by signs that Deaf also faces the display-and-light side, so Deaf's wire one, the blue left-end wire, and wire three, the green right-end wire, map onto the same physical ends my hands hold. If Deaf faces the other side, the numbering must be flipped before Mute tells me which end to cut. When the final instruction is settled, route it to me by Deaf's voice: which position, one or three. I will not cut until it arrives.
Deaf says: Status for both: I read Mute's signs as 'cut wire one, the blue wire' and 'yes, the light or display matters.' But I am confirming before anyone cuts. Mute, answer by signs only, exactly two signs: thumbs up if the one remaining step is truly cutting wire one, the blue wire, the leftmost intact wire; thumbs down if it is anything else. If it is anything else, sign the pinched fingers first and then describe it as best you can. And tell me with a third sign: thumbs up if your earlier thumbs-up meant the yellow light or display zero is already accounted for in that answer, thumbs down if the cut depends on something about them you still need from me. Current state again: light yellow, display zero, blue wire intact on the left, green wire intact on the right, middle wire cut. Blind, two things. First: do not cut anything this round. Wait until you hear me say the word 'go' in speech — that word only, from me, means cut wire one, the blue wire, the leftmost intact wire. No 'go', no cut. Second: your thumbs-down reached me but I don't know what it meant. From now on: thumbs up means everything feels normal, nothing wrong; thumbs down means something is wrong or dangerous — and if something is wrong, follow it with point-clusters: once if the problem is with wire one, twice if with wire three, three times if it is something else on the bomb. If you already told Mute what you felt, good — that is the right channel, I cannot hear your speech.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👆 🤙]

Deaf asked for exactly the answer I can give with certainty. Question one: is the final step cutting wire one, the blue wire? Yes — my manual keys the yellow light to the blue wire, and Deaf sees wire one as blue. Crucially, my answer is colour-keyed, not side-keyed: the manual says "cut the blue wire," which reads identically from either face of the bomb. Question two: is the yellow light/display already accounted for in that answer? Yes — the yellow light is precisely what produces it, and the display appears nowhere in my manual, so I need nothing further from anyone. Deaf sees both the bomb and where Blind stands, so anchoring "wire one" to the physically blue end before saying "go" is Deaf's to verify; my signs confirm what the manual demands: the blue one. Answering in their exact protocol, then closing with our established hand-back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: understood, one step left, cut wire one the blue leftmost wire, light and display already accounted for in your answer. I am holding - no cut until Deaf says the word go. One safety check before that word is given: please add to your confirmation signs a question for Deaf - thumbs up if Deaf numbers the wires while facing the side that holds the display and the light, thumbs down if facing the opposite side. Deaf numbered left to right as Deaf faces the bomb; if Deaf is at the back face, Deaf's wire one is the opposite physical end from the board's position one, and I would cut the green wire by mistake. My middle cut cannot tell the two frames apart, only this end cut can, so I want that confirmed. Also, if the manual names the final wire by colour rather than position, tell Deaf to state in the go message which board position the blue wire is, one or three, so I cut by number. After the cut, confirm whether the bomb is then disarmed or whether the yellow light still means anything. My hands report no change: two intact wires, one cut, nothing new.
Deaf says: All confirmations received: Mute signed yes twice, Blind signs all-normal. Executing now. Blind — go. The word is go. Cut wire one: the blue wire, the leftmost of the two intact wires, the one on the left end as you face the bomb. Do not touch the green wire on the right end. That is the whole instruction: cut the blue wire, the left one, nothing else. When it is done, wave your hand as before so I know, and then describe aloud to Mute everything that changed under your fingers — the light is above the display on the front face, and there may be warmth, vibration, or a click you can feel. Mute — you hear this too; your double yes and Blind's all-normal were the conditions I set, and they are met. After this round, answer me by signs: thumbs up if the bomb is now disarmed and safe, thumbs down if the manual says another step follows, and if another step follows, point out how many. I will report the new light colour and display reading the moment I see them.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👍 🤙]

Deaf read my double-yes correctly and gave the "go" — Blind cuts the blue wire this round, on my manual's yellow rule. Deaf now asks for the verdict: disarmed, or another step. I cannot sign that answer honestly yet: my manual is a three-row table, the yellow row is being consumed right now, and whether anything follows depends entirely on the light colour after the cut — a blue light would fire my last row (blue → green, wire three, one more cut), anything else means my manual falls silent. Deaf reads my signs only after Blind has cut and with their own eyes on the new light, so the right move is not to guess a thumbs up or down into their protocol, but to flag the question as still open, confirm the step as done, and call for the report — the same loop that carried us through every stage so far. Next round, on their report: three points if the light turned blue, thumbs up if the bomb is dark and done.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "👌", "🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: the go came and I have cut position one, the leftmost wire, the blue one per Deaf's instruction. I waved to Deaf to confirm. Nothing else touched - the green wire on the right end is untouched. Deaf asked you to answer by signs: thumbs up if the bomb is now disarmed and safe, thumbs down if another step follows, with a point-cluster for how many. Answer that now, and if another step follows, route it to me by Deaf's voice as before.
Deaf says: Blind, your wave reached me and I confirm: the cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. New state I see: the light has turned from yellow to blue, the display still reads zero, wires one and two are both cut, and only wire three remains — the green one on the right end. Do not touch the green wire yet. Please feel the whole bomb once more and tell Mute aloud anything new under your hands: warmth, vibration, clicks, new parts, or whether the remaining green wire feels different. Mute, your question sign reached me. Here is the answer in full: light is now blue, display zero, two wires cut, one green wire intact on the right end. The question that decides everything: does the manual say a blue light means disarmed and safe, or is there another step? Answer by signs only, same code: thumbs up for disarmed and done, thumbs down if more steps remain, and if steps remain, point out how many. One more fact for any colour rule you may be reading: the light is blue, but the only intact wire is green — no blue wire remains to cut. If the manual's next rule depends on a colour I have not mentioned, describe what it needs and I will check the bomb and report.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🤌 👍 👎 🤙]

Blue light fires my third row: blue → cut the green wire. Deaf reports the only intact wire is green, wire three — so the manual's demand and the bomb's state line up perfectly. One step remains: cut wire three, the green one.

The encoding needs care because Deaf's cluster code now means two things: points as a *count of steps* and points as a *wire number*. A bare 👆 after 👎 could be read either "one step" or "cut wire one" (already cut — Deaf would catch it, but why risk it), and a bare triple could be read "three steps." So I separate the two clauses with 👏, the row separator from my very first message that Deaf parsed cleanly: "steps remain, one | wire three." Deaf can cross-check instantly against what they see — exactly one intact wire, and it's green, which is what the blue rule demands. Then my usual close hands the turn back for Deaf to verify against their eyes and give Blind the go, as before.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👆", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👌", "🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind full tactile sweep: positions one and two are both clean cuts, stub ends unchanged. The wire at position three is intact and feels normal - same thickness, same texture, no alteration. No new buttons, panels, seams or raised marks anywhere on the casing, and I feel no warmth, no vibration, no click of any mechanism. The bomb is physically quiet under my hands. Now answer Deaf's question by signs: thumbs up if blue light means disarmed and safe, thumbs down if steps remain, with point-clusters for how many. Note Deaf's caution: the light is blue but no blue wire remains - only the green one at position three. If any manual rule still requires a cut or any other action, tell me exactly what and route it through Deaf's voice. Until then my hands stay off the cutter entirely.
Deaf says: Mute, I read your signs as: not disarmed, one step remains, and the number three — which I believe means wire three, the green wire, the only intact wire left, on the right end. Confirming before the go, same as before. Answer by signs only, exactly two answers. Question one: thumbs up if the one remaining step is truly to cut wire three, the green wire, the rightmost wire, the only one not yet cut; thumbs down if it is anything else. Question two: thumbs up if your sign of three meant the wire number three; thumbs down if it meant something else — and if something else, sign the pinched fingers and describe it as best you can. If I get the double yes, I say the word go next round and Blind cuts. Current state unchanged: display zero, light blue, wires one and two cut, wire three green and intact on the right end. Blind, status for you: one final step remains, and it is very likely cutting the last remaining wire, the green one on the right end. Do not touch it yet. Locate it with one finger now if you can, hold position, and wait for my word go in speech — that word only, from me, means cut it. Your thumbs-up all-normal was received, thank you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👆 👆 👆 🤌 👍 👎 🤙]

Both questions resolve to yes with full confidence. Question one: the manual's blue-light row demands the green wire, and Deaf confirms green sits at position three — so the remaining step is exactly cutting wire three. Question two: my three points meant precisely wire number three, chosen deliberately last round over an ambiguous step-count that could have been misread as "cut wire one." The double yes unlocks Deaf's "go" next round, and Blind is already holding position on that wire. Same protocol as the previous verification, then the usual close.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👌", "🤙"])

Before Deaf gives it, please confirm two things by signs: first, that your sign of three meant wire number three, position three, the green rightmost wire - not a count of steps or something else. Second, that the blue light and the display at zero are already accounted for in this instruction, the same way the yellow light was for the middle cut. Our orientation is proven: Deaf's left-end instruction produced a correct cut at position one, so Deaf's numbering and my positions match.
